context_guidance.home curbside: Follow the current accepted-material list from your curbside provider.
context_guidance.public bin: Read the labels on the public station because its collection options may differ from household bins.
context_guidance.workplace: Use the collection labels and instructions provided for your workplace.
context_guidance.community collection point: Ask the collection point whether it accepts this item before leaving it there.

rules.recommendation: Take it to an e-waste or battery collection point
rules.reason: Electronics and batteries can contain materials that are valuable to recover and harmful when they leak into household waste. Keep this item out of curbside bins and use a designated collection point.
rules.preparation: Keep batteries intact, cover exposed terminals when practical, and check your local collection service before drop-off.

rules.recommendation: Wrap securely and follow local broken-glass guidance
rules.reason: Loose broken glass can injure collection workers and is often excluded from glass recycling bins. Keep it separate from bottles and jars.
rules.preparation: Wrap the pieces in thick paper or cardboard, seal them in a sturdy container, and label it clearly.

rules.recommendation: Compost it where a suitable service is available
rules.reason: Food and garden scraps can become useful compost instead of taking up space in landfill. Accepted materials differ between home composters and municipal programs.
rules.preparation: Remove stickers and packaging. Keep meat, dairy, and oily foods out of a home compost pile unless your service explicitly accepts them.

rules.recommendation: Compost or place it in general waste, depending on local rules
rules.reason: Paper towels and tissues have short fibers that are generally unsuitable for paper recycling. Some organics programs accept them when they are free of harsh cleaners.
rules.preparation: Keep them out of the paper recycling bin. Check whether your compost service accepts used paper towels and tissues.

rules.recommendation: Compost the soiled part or place it in general waste
rules.reason: Food and grease can lower the quality of paper recycling. Some local compost programs accept uncoated food-soiled paper; others do not.
rules.preparation: Separate clean cardboard from greasy sections when possible, then check the accepted-material list for your local program.

rules.reason: Clean, dry paper fibers can usually be recovered into new paper products. Wet or food-soiled paper is harder to process.
rules.preparation: Keep it dry, flatten boxes, and remove plastic liners or excess tape when you can.

rules.recommendation: Use a soft-plastics collection point if available
rules.reason: Flexible films can tangle sorting equipment and are not accepted in many curbside recycling bins, even when the material is recyclable elsewhere.
rules.preparation: Keep the film clean and dry, bundle it only if your collection program asks you to, and check local drop-off options.

rules.recommendation: Recycle in the plastics bin if your local program accepts it
rules.reason: Rigid plastic containers such as PET bottles are commonly recyclable, but accepted resin types vary by location. A quick rinse helps keep other recyclables clean.
rules.preparation: Empty and rinse the container. Check local guidance for caps and labels, then place it loose in the recycling bin.

rules.recommendation: Empty and rinse it before recycling if accepted locally
rules.reason: Leftover food or liquid can contaminate a recycling load. If the item cannot be cleaned, follow local guidance for soiled packaging.
rules.preparation: Pour out liquids, scrape out food, and give the container a quick rinse. Do not recycle heavily contaminated packaging unless your local service permits it.

rules.recommendation: Recycle as glass if your local program accepts containers
rules.reason: Glass bottles and jars can often be recycled repeatedly, though some curbside programs do not collect glass or have separate drop-off sites.
rules.preparation: Empty and rinse the container. Keep drinking glasses, mirrors, ceramics, and window glass out of bottle-and-jar recycling.

rules.recommendation: Recycle with metal containers if accepted locally
rules.reason: Metal containers are widely recyclable, and recovering the material saves the resources needed to make new metal.
rules.preparation: Empty and rinse the can. Avoid flattening it unless your local program recommends that step.

rules.recommendation: Donate, repair, or use a textile collection program
rules.reason: Wearable items can have another life, and damaged textiles may be accepted by specialist collection programs. Textile collection options vary locally.
rules.preparation: Keep donated items clean and dry. If they are torn or worn out, check whether a textile recycler accepts them.

fallback.recommendation: Check the item label and your local waste guidance
fallback.reason: This item does not match a disposal rule with enough certainty. Packaging labels and local collection lists are the best next checks, especially for mixed-material items.
fallback.preparation: Keep hazardous or electronic items out of general waste until you confirm the correct collection route.
